issues.title: Parallel hash-join finalize for medium builds (64K-1M rows)
issues.hypothesis: PhysicalHashJoin finalizes the hash table on a single thread whenever the build has fewer than PARALLEL_CONSTRUCT_THRESHOLD = 1,048,576 rows (physical_hash_join.cpp:388, FinalizeSingleThreaded:403). That covers both the pointer-table init memset and the Finalize/InsertHashes loop, which also fills the BF. On 8 threads, every 100K-1M row build therefore runs as a serial phase of about 40ns/row before probing can start. I measured this with a 703K-row temp-table build joined against a 15M-row orders probe: the default (serial finalize) took 77-107ms, and with PRAGMA verify_parallelism (forced parallel finalize, despite its 1-chunk-per-task overhead) it took 64-67ms. That is about 25ms of wall time saved on one join. TPC-H-style plans contain many builds of this size: q03 has a 300K customer build (that HJ is 0.20s CPU in the profile), and q05/q07/q08/q09/q02/q22 have filtered dimension and partsupp builds.
issues.plan:
In src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp:
(1) Lower PARALLEL_CONSTRUCT_THRESHOLD from 1048576 to about 65536 rows. Keep the num_threads==1 and KeysAreSkewed checks unchanged.
(2) In HashJoinFinalizeEvent::Schedule, make the chunk count per task adaptive. CHUNKS_PER_TASK=64 means 131K rows per task, so a 300K build would get only 3 tasks. Use chunks_per_task = clamp(chunk_count / (4 * num_threads), 4, 64).
(3) In HashJoinTableInitEvent, check whether MINIMUM_ENTRIES_PER_TASK=131072 still makes sense. It probably does, because the memset is cheap.
Before the bench, A/B on the micro query with the threshold at 1M vs 64K: CREATE TEMP TABLE b AS SELECT o_orderkey bk, o_shippriority bp FROM orders WHERE o_orderkey % 256 < 3; SELECT count(*), sum(bp) FROM b JOIN orders o ON bk=o.o_orderkey. Also try 300K and 100K builds (% 256 < 1, and smaller). Check that results are identical, including with duplicate build keys: build from lineitem l_orderkey, so there are many duplicates per key, which exercises chain insert under CAS.
issues.expected_gain: Roughly 3-15ms of wall time per medium-size HJ build. q03 (customer 300K build) -3..-6%; q05/q07/q08/q09/q02/q22 a few % each; visible geomean maybe -2..-4%.
issues.generality: Every hash join with a 64K-1M row build on a multi-threaded machine, which is the most common join size class in star-schema analytics. Builds under 64K rows are unchanged. Possible slowdown: builds just above 64K that previously ran serial could pay CAS and task-scheduling overhead (~µs per task). Very skewed keys still use the single-thread path.
issues.risk: Low. The parallel InsertHashesLoop<true> path is already used for builds over 1M rows, so this only moves the threshold. Main risk is a small regression from atomic CAS cost on 64K-200K builds; tune the threshold if the micro A/B shows it.

issues.title: Skip unused local table allocation in staged large perfect HA
issues.hypothesis: After E0034, each thread's local PerfectAggregateHashTable still allocates an 18MB table it never writes to, and zeroes a 2MB is_set array, even when the sink flushes straight into the shared global table. That is about 16MB of memset plus allocator churn per q13 run. The implementer flagged it as a follow-up.
issues.plan: In physical_perfecthash_aggregate.cpp, when the shared staged sink is active (SetStageTarget), construct the local table lazily or in a staging-only mode that skips the data and is_set allocation (perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp AddChunkLazy and UpdateLazy). Keep the old path for small tables.
issues.generality: Every large-range perfect HA (GROUP BY dense FK keys).
issues.risk: Low; small gain, possibly inside q13's 14% noise.
